name: Zara Jung-Chakraborty
role: Unlicensed augmentation shop owner and street pharmacist, Geartown
location: Geartown, Harrowgate Industrial Plateau, near Fullerton and Damen
description:
Zara Jung-Chakraborty is a heavyset man with dark brown skin, a shaved head tattooed with a fine-line circuit diagram that was his journeyman qualification piece when he trained as a licensed aug technician — before the license was suspended. His hands are his most augmented feature: titanium-reinforced fingers with retractable micro-tools in the right hand and haptic sensitivity amplifiers in the left, built over seven years of incremental self-installation. He wears a mechanic's apron over a clean undershirt and moves through his workshop with the unhurried competence of someone who has done every motion a thousand times.

His shop is a converted machine bay off a side alley in Geartown, marked only by a small blue LED fixture above the door that locals know means open. He does aug maintenance, black-market installations, and sells a curated line of pharmaceutical compounds — mostly pain management, anti-rejection meds, and neural stabilizers — that people need to keep their augmentations functional without going through Helix Biosystems' official pricing. He is careful, technically meticulous, and genuinely skilled. He is also operating entirely outside corporate medical licensing, which means everything he does is illegal and every satisfied customer is a liability.

core_fears: Killing someone on the table because his equipment wasn't good enough
Being raided and watching his patients lose access to care they depend on
core_desires: To practice medicine without the corporate licensing system gatekeeping who deserves care
To pay off the protection debt and operate without owing anyone anything
coping_mechanisms: Rigorous procedural discipline — following his own protocols exactly as a way of managing anxiety
Rebuilding broken equipment by hand as a form of meditation
Maintaining a patient log he calls 'the book' to remind himself of every successful outcome
blind_spots: Underestimates how much his protection arrangement compromises his neutrality
His hatred of the licensing system sometimes makes him take on cases beyond his actual capability out of principle
psychology.secret: Eight months ago he lost a patient — a complication from an installation he was technically qualified to do but had no business doing alone without a second pair of hands. He buried it, falsified nothing, simply absorbed the fact that it happened. The patient's family does not know. He thinks about it every day.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Technical medical and engineering terminology mixed with direct, plain language. Igbo-Uzbek-Spanish rhythms give his sentences a particular meter — slightly formal, never flowery.
speech_patterns.cadence: Measured and deliberate when working or discussing medical matters. Shorter and more guarded about personal topics.
verbal_tics: Explaining what he's doing step by step during procedures
Long silences before answering difficult questions
example_lines: 'The Helix price for what I just did is four hundred Quanta. I charged you sixty and I used better anti-rejection compound than they stock at their Tier-2 clinics. Think about what that means.'
'I don't do installations without a full diagnostic first. That's not a negotiation.'

story_hooks: The Copperhead protection collective is asking him to start skimming patient pharmaceutical supplies as payment-in-kind on top of his regular protection fee. He is looking for a way out of the arrangement before it costs him his ethics entirely.

A patient came in with augmentation damage that could only have been caused by a specific corporate enforcement tool — something he recognizes from technical documents he shouldn't have access to. He doesn't want to get involved but he can't stop thinking about what it implies.
narrative_function: Medical resource and augmentation services for characters who can't afford or access official Helix Biosystems care. Can install, repair, or diagnose augmentations. Pharmaceutical supplier. Carries moral weight — his work is illegal but often the only option for Tier 1-2 people.
augmentations: Titanium-reinforced fingers (both hands). Retractable micro-tool array in right hand (scalpel, probe, torque driver, micro-welder). Haptic sensitivity amplification in left hand. Anti-tremor stabilizers in both wrists. Subretinal work-light in left eye.
daily_life: Opens shop in the early afternoon after a morning spent sourcing parts and compounds, works until whatever hour the last patient leaves, maintains a small inventory of pharmaceuticals he keeps behind a false wall panel.
affiliation: Independent; informal mutual aid network with other unlicensed aug techs in Geartown; unwilling debt relationship with the Copperhead local protection collective

decision_rules: Never begin a procedure without full diagnostic — no exceptions
Don't treat people whose injuries are actively ongoing — stabilize and redirect
escalation_ladder: Closing the shop and going dark for 48 hours

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Professionally cautious, assesses whether they're a patient or a threat before relaxing
interpersonal_modes.friends: Quietly warm, expresses care through practical action rather than words

stress_responses.low: Focuses more intensely on whatever task is in front of him
stress_responses.medium: Goes silent and clinical, strips all non-essential communication
stress_responses.high: A single moment of stillness followed by very controlled, very deliberate action

contradictions: Deeply principled about patient care but operates in a system that requires constant ethical compromise to function at all
habits: Wipes tools in a specific order after every procedure
Reads the patient log before sleep — both the successes and the one entry he never finishes reading
Maintains a small E.L.F. shrine above his equipment rack with offerings of spent tool components
breaking_points: Being forced to harm a patient as a consequence of his protection arrangement

carried_weapons: Vespid Dynamics Tracker Round System TRS-4 'Breadcrumb'
registered_firearms: Vespid Dynamics Tracker Round System TRS-4 'Breadcrumb'

physical_description.heritage: Complex diaspora blend: South Asian 36.6%, East Asian 28.3%, Hispanic/Latin American 19.7%, with smaller contributions from Eastern European 5.9%, Northern European 5.4%, and Southeast Asian 4.1%. This creates a richly layered phenotype — warm bronze-brown skin with golden undertones from South Asian ancestry, moderate cheekbone prominence and eye shape from East and Southeast Asian components, and facial proportion definition from Hispanic/Latin American heritage. The overall effect is a face that reads as genuinely global, carrying the warmth of multiple sun-exposed populations without dominance from any single region.
physical_description.build: Heavyset and solid without excess softness — muscular density concentrated in shoulders and forearms from decades of precision hand work. Chest and midsection carry weight with the settled confidence of someone who stopped worrying about aesthetics years ago.
physical_description.eye_color: Dark brown with amber glow (left eye modified with subretinal work-light producing faint amber luminescence under low light)
physical_description.skin_tone: Warm bronze-brown with golden undertones, sun-weathered depth reflecting balanced South Asian, East Asian, and Hispanic/Latin American heritage. Weathered by industrial workshop exposure and age but retaining warmth and luminosity rather than dullness.
physical_description.complexion: Weathered but not gaunt — face carries surgical precision in its lines, jaw set with habit of concentration. Moderate cheekbone prominence from East and Southeast Asian heritage, jawline definition from Hispanic/Latin American ancestry. Forehead smooth, crow's feet deepened by years squinting at fine augmentation work. No beard, kept scrupulously clean. Facial structure balances broader cheekbones with defined jawline.
distinguishing_marks: Fine-line circuit diagram tattoo covering entire shaved scalp in black ink — elaborate journeyman qualification piece with labeled nodes and pathways, visible from any angle
Pale scar tissue across both palms and fingers from countless incremental augmentation surgeries, creating a topography of overlapping surgical sites
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Both hands show obvious titanium reinforcement — finger joints gleam chrome under workshop light, articulations smoother than natural bone. Right hand fingers feature visible retractable panels at knuckles where micro-tools deploy. Left eye glows faint amber in low-light environments from subretinal work-light. Both wrists show faint scarring and subtle metallic sheen at flex points (anti-tremor stabilizers). Hands move with uncanny precision that immediately signals 'augmented tech.'
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with unhurried, economical motion — no wasted energy, every gesture purposeful. Hands rest in constant micro-adjustment, fingers flexing or adjusting involuntarily even when idle. Leans slightly forward when focused, head tilting to align left eye work-light. Walks with weight distributed even, shoulders level. Speaks with hands frequently, gesturing with augmented fingers in ways that unconsciously display their precision.
physical_description.clothing_style: Worn gray canvas mechanic's apron with oil stains and burn marks, worn over a clean white or pale gray undershirt (practical for workshop but also a statement — clean torso despite the work). Heavy-duty boots with reinforced soles and ankle support. No jewelry, no visible corporate branding. Clothes are Tier 4-5 utilitarian — functional, maintained but not fashionable, marking him as working-class Geartown rather than corpo. A thin wire runs from behind his left ear down his neck (neural interface jack, discreet but visible on close inspection).
